newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NRG Australia in Indonesia power deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NRG Australia in Indonesia power deal.

text.p: NRG Australia Ltd, a unit of Northern States Power Co, said on Thursday it and the Ansaldo Group of Italy had won a A$600 million contract to build and operate a 400-megawatt power station in West Java, Indonesia.

The joint venture won the contract ahead of Mitsubishi Corp of Japan and the U.S.-based Duke Energy to become the first tender contract under Indonesia's private power programme, NRG Australia executive director Craig Cooper told Reuters.
"The contract is the largest Australian-led power project and will operate and maintain the power station for 30 years," Cooper said. The plant will use Indonesian-sourced coal.
Cooper said NRG Australia and Ansaldo would each have a 45 percent stake in the project with Ansaldo responsible for all electro-mechanical work at the plant.
NRG Australia's Indonesian subsidiary PT NRG West Java will be operator in conjunction with NRG's Indonesian associate PT Kiana Metra, which will hold a 10 percent stake, Cooper said.
He said the power station would have a 38-month construction schedule starting in the first quarter of next year.
Commissioning of the power station would be in February 2000 with operation starting the following month.
NRG Australia's interests include a 38 percent stake in the Gladstone power station consortium and 50 percent of the Collinsville power station in Queensland.
NRG was also among bidders for the Hazlewood and Yallourn power stations in Victoria.
